Here's the U.S. Core Inflation Rate (Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers: All Items Less Food & Energy) from January 2015 to December 2016, presented in a Markdown table:

| Month      | Year | Core Inflation Rate (YoY % Change) |
|--------------|------|------------------------------------|
| January      | 2015 | 1.6%                              |
| February     | 2015 | 1.7%                              |
| March        | 2015 | 1.8%                              |
| April        | 2015 | 1.8%                              |
| May          | 2015 | 1.7%                              |
| June         | 2015 | 1.8%                              |
| July         | 2015 | 1.8%                              |
| August       | 2015 | 1.8%                              |
| September    | 2015 | 1.8%                              |
| October      | 2015 | 1.9%                              |
| November     | 2015 | 2.0%                              |
| December     | 2015 | 2.1%                              |
| January      | 2016 | 2.2%                              |
| February     | 2016 | 2.3%                              |
| March        | 2016 | 2.2%                              |
| April        | 2016 | 2.2%                              |
| May          | 2016 | 2.3%                              |
| June         | 2016 | 2.3%                              |
| July         | 2016 | 2.2%                              |
| August       | 2016 | 2.3%                              |
| September    | 2016 | 2.2%                              |
| October      | 2016 | 2.2%                              |
| November     | 2016 | 2.1%                              |
| December     | 2016 | 2.2%                              |

**Source:** Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), Consumer Price Index (CPI) data.  You can find this data on the BLS website (bls.gov).  This data represents the year-over-year percentage change for each month.  It is the most recent data available to me as of my knowledge cutoff.
